claim.pdf_says: (page 857 ends with H.2 item 4) "... This error has not been fixed because the PADDING CHARACTER clause is obsolete." -- no further heading is printed on the page
claim.why_it_matters: The markdown adds a top-level heading that the PDF does not print anywhere, at the end of Annex H page 857. The printed Bibliography heading is on page 858 and the Index heading is on page 859. The invented level-1 heading changes the document's outline, so Annex H content seems to sit under a section that does not exist.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 857 (folio 835) does end with H.2 item 4 and prints no further heading, and every word of the page is present in the markdown. The '# Bibliography and index' line is not transcribed content. It is one of the transcription's five level-1 grouping headings ('# Preface', '# Front matter: covers, contents, foreword and introduction', '# Clauses 1 to 16', '# Annexes A to H', '# Bibliography and index', at lines 1, 35, 859, 25713 and 33207 of the 2002 markdown), none of which the PDF prints. It sits right before '## Page 858', so it opens the group that holds page 858 ('### Bibliography') and page 859 ('### Index'). It shows up in page 857's slice only because the page splitter runs up to the next '## Page' marker. Annex H content is not placed under it: the Annex H text comes before it, under '# Annexes A to H'. This is document scaffolding with no change to the standard's content, so it is not a discrepancy.
